entries.ae885e114ad2a83afe08ac1e5f05d43002706f79: <reference osisRef="Job.32.18-Job.22.18">Job 32:18-22 18</reference>  For I am full of words, <div eID="gen8342" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8343" type="x-p"/> The spirit of my inner nature constraineth me. 19  Behold, my interior is like wine which is not opened, <div eID="gen8343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8344" type="x-p"/> Like new bottles it is ready to burst. 20  I will speak, that I may gain air, <div eID="gen8344" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8345" type="x-p"/> I will open my lips and reply. 21  No, indeed, I will accept no man’s person, <div eID="gen8345" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8346" type="x-p"/> And I will flatter no man. 22  For I understand not how to flatter; <div eID="gen8346" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8347" type="x-p"/> My Maker would easily snatch me away. <div eID="gen8347" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8348" type="x-p"/> The young speaker continues still further his declaration, promising so much. He has a rich store of מלּים, words, i.e., for replying. מלתי defective for מלאתי, like יצתי for יצאתי, <reference osisRef="Job.1.21">Job 1:21</reference>; whereas מלוּ, <reference osisRef="Ezek.28.6">Eze 28:6</reference>, is not only written defectively, but is also conjugated after the manner of a <hi type="italic">Lamed He</hi> verb, Ges. §§23, 3, 74, rem. 4, 75, 21, c. The spirit of his inner nature constrains him, since, on account of its intensity and the fulness of this interior, it struggles to break through as through a space that is too narrow for it. בּטן, as <reference osisRef="Job.15.2">Job 15:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.15.35">Job 15:35</reference>, not from the curved appearance of the belly, but from the interior of the body with its organs, which serve the spirit life as the strings of a harp; comp. Arab. <hi type="italic">batn</hi>, the middle or interior; <hi type="italic">bâtin</hi>, inwardly (opposite of <hi type="italic">zâhir</hi>, outwardly). His interior is like wine לא יפּתח, which, or (as an adverbial dependent clause) when it is not opened, i.e., is kept closed, so that the accumulated gas has no vent, lxx δεδεμένος (bound up), Jer. <hi type="italic">absque spiraculo;</hi> it will burst like new bottles. יבּקע is not a relative clause referring distributively to each single one of these bottles (Hirz. and others), and not an adverbial subordinate clause (Hahn: when it will explode), but predicate to בטני: his interior is near bursting like new bottles (אבות <hi type="italic">masc</hi>. like נאדות, <reference osisRef="Josh.9.13">Jos 9:13</reference>), i.e., not such as are themselves new (ἀσκοὶ καινοὶ, <reference osisRef="Matt.9.17">Mat 9:17</reference>, for these do not burst so easily), but like bottles of new wine, which has to undergo the action of fermentation, lxx ὥσπερ φυσητὴρ (<hi type="italic">Cod. Sinait.1</hi> φυσητής) χαλκέως, i.e., חרשׁים whence it is evident that a bottle and also a pair of bellows were called אוב). Since he will now yield to his irresistible impulse, in order that he may obtain air or free space, i.e., disburdening and ease (וירוח לּי), he intends to accept no man’s person, i.e., to show partiality to no one (vid., on <reference osisRef="Job.13.8">Job 13:8</reference>), and he will flatter no one. כּנּה signifies in all three dialects to call any one by an honourable name, to give a surname, here with אל, to speak fine words to any one, to flatter him. This Elihu is determined he will not do; for לא ידעתּי אכנּה, I know not how to flatter (French, <hi type="italic">je ne sais point flatter</hi>), for כנּות or לכנּות; comp. the similar constructions, <reference osisRef="Job.23.3">Job 23:3</reference> (as <reference osisRef="Esth.8.6">Est 8:6</reference>), <reference osisRef="Job.10.16">Job 10:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.3">1Sa 2:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.42.21">Isa 42:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.51.1">Isa 51:1</reference>, Ges. 142, 3, c; also in Arabic similar verbs, as “to be able” and “to prepare one’s self,” are thus connected with the <hi type="italic">fut</hi>. without a particle between (e.g., <hi type="italic">anshaa jef‛alu ,</hi> he began to act). Without partiality he will speak, flattery is not his force. If by flattery he should deny the truth, his Maker would quickly carry him off. כּמעט followed by subjunct. <hi type="italic">fut.:</hi> for a little (with disjunctive accent, because equivalent to <hi type="italic">haud multum abest quin</hi>), i.e., very soon indeed, or easily would or might ... ; ישּׂני (as <reference osisRef="Job.27.21">Job 27:21</reference>) seems designedly to harmonize with עשׂני.  <chapter eID="Job.32"/> <div eID="gen8348" type="x-p"/>
